target_customer: AI-native developers and engineering teams shipping coding agents and AI agents, with a free tier for open source projects
problem: Teams merging AI-written code and running autonomous agents have no reliable way to check changes, bound what agents can do, or show users the system is safe.
business_model: Open-source core plus hosted usage-based security services, free for open source; a guard model priced per million tokens per a third-party review

founders.name: Alan Zabihi
founders.background_notes: YC page and company about page name him CEO; neither lists background.

founders.name: Ismail Pelaseyed
founders.background_notes: Ships the open-source Superagent repo and speaks publicly on agent security; background not listed on the YC page or company page I opened.

technical_complexity.rationale: At founding the product was an open-source framework for building agents, standard LLM application engineering. The later security pivot adds adversarial testing and a small guard model, which is harder but still within reach of a two person team.

defensibility.rationale: Open-source code with many similar guardrail libraries and a crowded LLM security field, so copying a framework was easy; the main asset is developer mindshare.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: A third-party roundup says Check Point bought Lakera in September 2025 and SentinelOne bought Prompt Security, showing incumbents consolidated the category after the batch. No source shows Superagent itself being copied or bought.

market_need_then: Prompt injection and data leaks from LLM agents were becoming a known concern around 2024, though paying demand for agent security was still forming; evidence of spend at the time is not sourced.

branding.domain_note: Uses superagent.sh, a .sh domain; the founder's GitHub profile lists it with an @superagent.sh email. Purchase history not found.

identity.visual_style: Plain developer-tool site with numbered sections and customer quotes
identity.voice_and_tone: Short, plain, confident sentences such as 'The autonomous security factory'

rebrands.from: Superagent as open-source framework for building AI assistants
rebrands.to: Superagent as runtime security for AI agents
rebrands.why: Repositioning toward agent security; a 2026 review dates the runtime product launch to October 1, 2025. Name unchanged.

branding.community_and_virality: The open-source repo has an active developer following and the founder appears on developer podcasts in 2026; no merch or meme evidence found.

brand_strength.rationale: A generic word that other products also use, with moderate open-source awareness. No press about the brand itself was found.

pivots.from: Open-source framework for building AI assistants and agents
pivots.to: Security for AI agents: runtime defense, red teaming and pull request checks
pivots.why: A 2026 review and the company site show the shift to agent security; the founders' stated reason was not found.

outcome_analysis: Superagent is still active as a two person team. It began as an open-source agent framework, then repositioned toward agent security in late 2025 as prompt injection concerns grew. No verified funding amount or acquisition was found, so the outcome is undetermined; competitors in the category were acquired in 2025, which suggests the market is real but crowded.
notes: Funding unverified: CB Insights and VCBacked (aggregators) list a 0.5M convertible note around January 2024 with Y Combinator; EveryDev lists 1.6M, which conflicts. The company about page says it is backed by Y Combinator and Rebel Fund plus founders of Okta, Replit and HubSpot, with no amounts. No competitor source dated near the W24 batch was found. An aggregator mentions an Airtable acquisition that I could not confirm and may refer to a different entity. Founding year: YC says 2024, StartupHub says 2023. Completeness pass: one convertible note of 500K dated 2024-01 is recorded from CB Insights alone (CB Insights says 500K over 2 rounds); it rests on a single database. VCBacked calls it pre-seed announced February 2024, EveryDev says 1.6M and Startups.fm says 2.5M, which conflict and are not recorded.
